newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade slow at $64 -feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade slow at $64 -feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle near midday Thursday sold in light volume at $64.00 per cwt, unchanged from the bulk of Wednesday's active sales, feedlot sources and USDA said.

About 2,100 head of steers and heifers that will likely grade select and choice sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area, according to USDA. Week-to-date sales were estimated at 91,600, including 23,700 formulated and 900 previously contracted cattle to be shipped this week.
About 4,000 head of cattle that will likely grade select to choice sold in Kansas Thursday morning, USDA said.
The week-to-date number for Kansas near midday was pegged by USDA at 79,800 head, including 23,500, or about 29 percent previously contracted or formulated cattle.
Early bids at $63.00 were passed by owners who would lose money if they sold cattle under $64.00, sources said.
"Even at $64.00, it's nip and tuck, with more (owners) in the red than in the black," one Kansas feedlot manager said.
Packers reportedly were faced with tighter operating margins this week following the recent skid in beef prices, sources said.
